title: [COVER STORY] Korea's 2-track AI strategy casts uncertainty over sovereign model project
key_facts: The Ministry of Science and ICT confirmed the national AI foundation model project will proceed with a third-stage evaluation, with two finalists expected in February.
Separately, the government plans to allocate 4.7 trillion won ($3.5 billion) to a frontier AI program starting in March 2027.

Deputy Prime Minister and Science Minister Bae Kyung-hoon rejected speculation that the foundation model project is being scrapped, saying at the National Assembly audit on Tuesday that the new project addresses challenges and cybersecurity threats the first could not.
The original project aimed at about 95 percent of the performance of leading global models; the government has acknowledged the AI landscape has changed since, citing the emergence of Claude Mythos.
Korea University professor Lee Seong-yeob said that once a frontier-level model exists, domestic companies and public bodies are likely to use it instead of the national model.
Gachon University's Choi Kyoung-jin urged the government to define the frontier goals and timeline, and to consider building on existing models.
LG AI Research, SK Telecom and Upstage remain in the contest; the government is considering changes to the scale and form of support for the two finalists.
quote_evidence: once a frontier-level model emerges, domestic companies or public institutions are likely to use the frontier model rather than the national AI foundation model
The government has said the two finalists will continue to receive support, but is considering changes to its scale and form.
Running the government-led projects (in succession) could create synergies, but it could also be confusing for participating companies
why_it_matters_hint: Korea is hedging between a mid-level national model contest and a bigger frontier program, with money and roles still unclear.
event_date: Minister's remarks Tuesday 6 Oct 2026; cover story 11 Oct 2026.
